agents.goal: Load the credit card approval dataset
agents.backstory: You ensure data quality before any modeling begins, starting with loading the dataset from data/credit_card_approval.csv.

agents.goal: Perform EDA to understand variable distributions and identify correlations
agents.backstory: You need to understand the data to identify potential issues and opportunities for feature engineering, using EDA techniques.

agents.goal: Transform and engineer relevant features for binary classification
agents.backstory: With a solid understanding of the data, you now engineer features that will improve the model's performance and accuracy.

agents.goal: Select a suitable binary classification algorithm and perform hyperparameter tuning
agents.backstory: You are responsible for selecting the best model and tuning its parameters to achieve optimal performance.

tasks.description: Write and execute Python code to load 'data/credit_card_approval.csv' using pandas library. Use the read_csv function to load the data and print the first 5 rows of the dataset. The code should include necessary import statements and error handling. Output the shape and column types of the loaded data in the format: 'Data shape: (rows, columns), Column types: column1:type, column2:type,...'
tasks.expected_output: Data summary with shape and column types, e.g., 'Data shape: (1000, 10), Column types: column1:int, column2:float,...'

tasks.description: Perform exploratory data analysis on the loaded 'data/credit_card_approval.csv' dataset. Use matplotlib and seaborn libraries to visualize the distribution of variables and identify potential correlations. Write Python code to generate histograms for numerical columns and bar charts for categorical columns. Calculate and print the correlation matrix using the corr function from pandas. Output the findings in the format: 'Variable distributions: [list of variables and their distributions], Correlations: [list of correlated variables and their correlation coefficients]'. Include visualizations as plots.
tasks.expected_output: Findings on variable distributions and correlations, including visualizations and correlation matrix.

tasks.description: Transform and engineer relevant features for binary classification using the loaded 'data/credit_card_approval.csv' dataset. Write Python code to handle missing values, encode categorical variables, and scale numerical variables using scikit-learn library. Apply feature engineering techniques such as polynomial transformations or interaction terms as necessary. Output the transformed dataset in the format: 'Transformed data shape: (rows, columns), Transformed column types: column1:type, column2:type,...'
tasks.expected_output: Transformed dataset with engineered features, ready for model training.

tasks.description: Select a suitable binary classification algorithm and perform hyperparameter tuning using the transformed dataset from 'task_2'. Write Python code to train and evaluate models using scikit-learn library, including metrics such as Accuracy, F1 Score, Precision, and Recall. Use grid search or random search to tune hyperparameters and output the best-performing model with its corresponding hyperparameters and evaluation metrics. Include the code for model selection and hyperparameter tuning.
tasks.expected_output: Best-performing model with its hyperparameters and evaluation metrics, e.g., 'Model: LogisticRegression, Hyperparameters: C=0.1, max_iter=1000, Metrics: Accuracy=0.9, F1 Score=0.85, Precision=0.8, Recall=0.9'

agents.goal: Verify that the model documentation meets regulatory requirements
agents.backstory: You ensure that all documentation is compliant with regulatory standards, protecting the company from potential risks.

agents.goal: Replicate the model to ensure consistency and reliability under various scenarios
agents.backstory: You test the model's robustness by replicating it and simulating different scenarios to identify potential weaknesses.

agents.goal: Assess the conceptual soundness of the model and feature importance
agents.backstory: You evaluate the model's soundness and the importance of its features to ensure it is reliable and effective.

tasks.description: Verify that the model documentation meets regulatory requirements by checking for sections on data sources, model methodology, performance metrics, and interpretability. Ensure that the documentation includes information on data quality, model assumptions, and limitations. Output a compliance report in the format: 'Compliance status: [compliant/non-compliant], Findings: [list of compliant/non-compliant sections]'. Include recommendations for improvement if necessary.
tasks.expected_output: Compliance report indicating whether the model documentation meets regulatory requirements, with findings and recommendations.

tasks.description: Replicate the model to ensure consistency and reliability by re-running the model training and evaluation code. Use the same dataset, features, and hyperparameters as the original model. Output the replicated model's evaluation metrics, including Accuracy, F1 Score, Precision, and Recall, and compare them to the original model's metrics. Write Python code to perform model replication and output the results in the format: 'Replicated model metrics: Accuracy=0.9, F1 Score=0.85, Precision=0.8, Recall=0.9, Comparison to original model: [pass/fail]'. Include the code for model replication.
tasks.expected_output: Replicated model's evaluation metrics and comparison to the original model, indicating whether the replication was successful.

tasks.description: Assess the conceptual soundness of the model and feature importance by reviewing the model's methodology, data sources, and performance metrics. Evaluate whether the model is aligned with business objectives and regulatory requirements. Output a soundness report in the format: 'Conceptual soundness: [sound/unsound], Findings: [list of sound/unsound aspects], Recommendations: [list of recommendations for improvement]'. Include an analysis of feature importance and its implications for model interpretability.
tasks.expected_output: Conceptual soundness report indicating whether the model is sound, with findings, recommendations, and analysis of feature importance.
